newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DAIMLER CHAIRMAN SAYS AFRICA MARKET OF THE FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: DAIMLER CHAIRMAN SAYS AFRICA MARKET OF THE FUTURE.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG Chairman Juergen Schrempp said on Saturday German industry was committed to development in Southern Africa and hoped to promote the region's swift integration into the global market.
"While pessimists may regard Africa as the lost continent, we see it as the market of the future," Schrempp said in a prepared address to the South African-German Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

Schrempp, who heads up the Southern Africa Initiative of German Business (SAFRI), pledged the organisation's support for regional integration by providing expertise, technology transfers and advice on trade and business to the 12 members of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) trade bloc.

"It will not help South Africa much if we build a handful of ultra-modern factories and expect them to be globally successful tomorrow. It makes much more sense for us to help develop the economic potential of SADC and each of its member nations," he said.

Applauding the South African government's determination to adhere to its market-oriented macro-economic strategy, he called on lender nations to invest in the future of Southern Africa by waving the debts incurred by previous colonial regimes.

But he cautioned that enduring political and economic stability was a prerequisite for the massive direct investment needed from abroad to underpin social peace in the region and tackle South Africa's severe unemployment problem.
Schrempp returns to Germany for next week's German/South African Binational Commission conference in Bonn, where Pretoria's Finance Minister Trevor Manuel will deliver the keynote address.

Currently, there are over 350 German companies established in South Africa with more than 70,000 employees. In 1996 the total foreign trade volume with Germany amounted to over 23 billion rand ($5 billion), two-thirds of which comprised German exports.
